## Structure becomes visible

A figure can bring several scales of an explanation into view. Here, material properties and stress fields sit beside electronic structure and crystal geometry. Each panel keeps its own axes, units and source.

![](../fig/renders/fig-1.svg){#fig-1}

The plate combines typical reference values, calculations and illustrative models. It is a visual study, not a report of one experiment. The crystal structures come from the Crystallography Open Database; the MgB₂ geometry uses the FermiSurfer example data @fermisurfer.

## From individual cells to a population

The neuroscience plate brings anatomy together with responses of 143 visual neurons recorded by the Allen Brain Observatory @allen-observatory. A response atlas keeps individual cells visible; population trajectories offer a complementary view of their shared activity.

![](../fig/renders/fig_mut5bjopik7r_124.svg){#fig-fig-mut5bjopik7r-124}

The anatomical models and functional recordings are separate specimens. The network connects similar response profiles, not anatomically connected neurons. MICrONS reconstructions provide examples of neuronal form.

## An explanation can move

At three stimulus frequencies, the same cells occupy different positions in a common response space. The embedded slide preserves each cell's identity as the view changes. Interpolation helps follow the transition; it does not add measured time points.

![](../slides/website-showcase/renders/response-geometry-step-0.svg){#slide-response-story .flux-slide deck="website-showcase" slide="response-geometry" width=100%}
